q.s: The Early Harappan phase of about 3300-2600 BCE, marked by distinct regional pottery styles, is called the:
q.x: The Early Harappan phase (3300-2600 BCE) is the Regionalisation Era; the Mature Harappan phase is the Integration Era and the Late Harappan the Localisation Era.

q.s: Which of the following sites does NOT show an Early (Pre-) Harappan phase?
q.x: Amri, Kot Diji and Kalibangan have Early Harappan levels; Lothal is a Mature Harappan port town.

q.s: The Harappan site of Banawali in Haryana was excavated by:
q.x: R. S. Bisht excavated Banawali (1973-74); Amarendra Nath worked at Rakhigarhi and Bopardikar at Daimabad.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in Haryana?
q.x: Daimabad is in Maharashtra on the Pravara; the others are in Haryana.

q.s: Who was the first to describe the ruins of Harappa, in 1826?
q.x: Charles Masson described Harappa in 1826; Cunningham visited it in 1853 and 1856, and Fleet published Harappan seals in 1912.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the discovery of Harappa is correct?
o: John Marshall published Harappan seals in 1912
Alexander Cunningham visited Harappa in the 1850s and saw a seal
q.x: Cunningham visited Harappa in 1853 and 1856. Fleet published the seals in 1912, and Daya Ram Sahni excavated Harappa in 1921.

q.s: The Harappan site of Daimabad in Maharashtra is located on the bank of the river:
q.x: Daimabad lies on the Pravara, a tributary of the Godavari.

q.s: Manda, the northernmost Harappan site in Jammu, lies on the river:
q.x: Manda is on the Chenab near Jammu.

q.s: The Buddhist stupa at Bhattiprolu in Guntur district was excavated by:
q.x: Alexander Rea excavated Bhattiprolu; Burgess worked at Amaravati and Jaggayyapeta, and Longhurst at Nagarjunakonda.

q.s: Which of the following archaeologists is NOT associated with excavating a Buddhist site in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Wheeler excavated Arikamedu near Puducherry; Burgess worked at Amaravati, Rea at Bhattiprolu and Longhurst at Nagarjunakonda.

q.s: The Rajatarangini, a Sanskrit chronicle of the kings of Kashmir written in the 12th century, was composed by:
q.x: Kalhana wrote it under Jayasimha of Kashmir; Jonaraja and Srivara later continued it.

q.s: Kalhana's Rajatarangini was continued by all of the following EXCEPT:
q.x: Jonaraja, Srivara and Prajyabhatta continued it; Bilhana wrote the Vikramankadevacharita.

q.s: Which of the following is regarded as the first Telugu inscription?
q.x: The Kalamalla inscription of the Renati Chodas is the first Telugu inscription; Bhattiprolu inscriptions are in Prakrit/Brahmi.

q.s: Which inscription is the first to mention the Kakatiyas?
q.x: The Magallu inscription first mentions the Kakatiyas; the Kazipet inscription names Beta Raja I as the first Kakatiya king.

q.s: The Brahmanas, prose texts that explain the Vedic hymns and sacrifices, belong to which part of Vedic literature?
q.x: Explaining sacrifices (karma), the Brahmanas with the Samhitas form the Karma-kanda; the Upanishads form the Jnana-kanda.

q.s: Which of the following led the Ajivika sect and was a contemporary of the Buddha?
q.x: Makkhali Gosala led the Ajivikas; Alara Kalama was a teacher of Siddhartha.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Alara Kalama and Uddaka Ramaputta taught Siddhartha before his enlightenment
Makkhali Gosala was a disciple of the Buddha
The Buddha attained enlightenment at Sarnath
The Buddha nominated Ananda as head of the Sangha after his death
q.x: Alara Kalama and Uddaka Ramaputta were his teachers; the Buddha named no successor, and he attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya.

q.s: In the structure of a stupa, the hemispherical dome is called the:
q.x: Anda is the dome; Harmika the square railing on top, Yashti the mast and Vedika the railing round the stupa.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of a Buddhist stupa?
q.x: The gopuram is the gateway tower of a South Indian temple, not a part of the stupa.

q.s: According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, the normal annual rate of interest in the Mauryan period was:
q.x: The Arthashastra fixes interest at 15 per cent a year (1.25 per cent a month).

q.s: The typical pottery of the Mauryan period was:
q.x: NBPW is the characteristic pottery of the Mauryan age; PGW is linked with the later Vedic period.

q.s: The Mehrauli iron pillar of the Gupta period has not rusted for over fifteen centuries mainly because:
o: It is coated with a layer of copper
Its high-phosphorus iron forms a protective film
It is made of chromium steel
q.x: The high phosphorus content of the iron forms a thin protective (passive) film on the surface.

q.s: The Dasakumaracharita and the Kavyadarsha were written by:
q.x: Dandin wrote both; Bhatti wrote the Ravanavadha (Bhattikavya), Bharavi the Kiratarjuniya and Magha the Shishupalavadha.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Dandin?
q.x: The Ravanavadha (Bhattikavya) is Bhatti's work.

q.s: The village assemblies sabha and ur, on which the Cholas built their local self-government, already appear under the:
q.x: The sabha and ur appear under the Pallavas and were developed by the Cholas.

q.s: The historian Burton Stein described the Chola state as a:
q.x: Burton Stein called it a segmentary state; Nilakanta Sastri saw it as centralised with vigorous local self-government.

q.s: Malik Kafur invaded Warangal in 1309-10 during the reign of the Kakatiya ruler:
q.x: Prataparudra was the Kakatiya king when Malik Kafur besieged Warangal in 1309-10 and made him a tributary.

q.s: The first attack of the Delhi army on Warangal (1303) under Malik Fakhruddin Juna was defeated at:
q.x: Potuganti Maili and Recherla Venna defeated the Delhi army at Upparapalli in 1303.

q.s: Rana Sanga of Mewar defeated Ibrahim Lodi in 1517 at the battle of:
q.x: Rana Sanga beat Ibrahim Lodi at Khatoli in 1517; Khanwa (1527) was his defeat by Babur.

q.s: Rajon ki Baoli, the stepwell at Mehrauli, was built in 1506 during the reign of:
q.x: Rajon ki Baoli dates from 1506, in Sikandar Lodi's reign.

q.s: Which Delhi Sultan was known for his orthodoxy, destroying temples at Mathura and imposing jizya?
q.x: Sikandar Lodi was orthodox: he destroyed temples at Mathura, broke the Nagarkot images and imposed jizya.

q.s: Which of the following rulers did NOT belong to the Lodi dynasty?
q.x: Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid dynasty (1414).

q.s: Muhammad Qasim Ferishta wrote his Tarikh-i-Ferishta (Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi) at the court of:
q.x: Ferishta wrote at the Bijapur court of Ibrahim Adil Shah II.

q.s: Which of the following historians did NOT write about the fall of Warangal in 1323?
q.x: Ferishta, Isami and Barani describe the fall of Warangal; Abul Fazl was Akbar's historian.

q.s: The Dahsala system of land revenue, introduced by Akbar in 1580, was the work of:
q.x: Raja Todar Mal devised the Dahsala (1580).

q.s: Under the Dahsala system, revenue was fixed on the basis of the average produce and prices of the previous:
q.x: It averaged the produce and prices of the ten years 1571-80; the dasturs were cash rates.

q.s: In 1632 Shah Jahan drove which European traders out of Hughli for their trading abuses?
q.x: Shah Jahan attacked and expelled the Portuguese from Hughli in 1632.

q.s: The white-marble Moti Masjid inside the Red Fort, Delhi, was built by:
q.x: Aurangzeb built the Moti Masjid of the Red Fort; Shah Jahan built the Moti Masjid of Agra Fort.

q.s: Which of the following buildings was NOT built by Shah Jahan?
q.x: Akbar built the Allahabad Fort (1583).

q.s: Ram Bagh, one of the earliest Mughal gardens in India, was laid out by Babur at:
q.x: Babur laid out the Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh) at Agra.

q.s: Which of the following monuments is the earliest?
q.x: Agra Fort was begun in 1565, Char Minar built in 1591, the Taj begun in 1632 and the Jama Masjid in 1650.

q.s: The Char Minar at Hyderabad (1591) was built by:
q.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built the Char Minar in 1591 when he founded Hyderabad.

q.s: The first Jesuit mission from Goa reached Akbar's court in 1580 under:
q.x: Rudolf Acquaviva led the first mission (1580); Jerome Xavier came with the third mission (1595).

q.s: Which of the following statements about Akbar and the Jesuits is correct?
o: The Jesuits brought the Polyglot Bible, whose pictures Akbar showed to his painters
The first Jesuit mission reached Akbar in 1595
European pictures first reached Akbar's court through Danish merchants
The Jesuit missions to Akbar came from Pondicherry
q.x: The Polyglot Bible's pictures were shown to Akbar's painters. European pictures came through the Portuguese Jesuits, and the first mission came from Goa in 1580.

q.s: Sena, one of the disciples of Ramananda, was by profession a:
q.x: Sena was a barber; Kabir was a weaver and Raidas a cobbler.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a disciple of Ramananda?
q.x: Chaitanya was a Bengal Vaishnava saint unconnected with Ramananda.

q.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, who propounded Wahdat-ush-Shuhud, belonged to the Sufi order of:
q.x: Sirhindi was a Naqshbandi, disciple of Khwaja Baqi Billah.

q.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi opposed all of the following EXCEPT:
q.x: Sirhindi propounded Wahdat-ush-Shuhud; he was imprisoned by Jahangir in the Gwalior Fort.

q.s: The term 'Ganimi Kava', associated with the Marathas under Shivaji, refers to:
q.x: Ganimi Kava was guerrilla warfare with swift cavalry in the Sahyadri hills.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of Shivaji's Ashtapradhan?
q.x: Mir Bakshi was a Mughal office; the Ashtapradhan included the Peshwa, Amatya, Sachiv, Mantri, Senapati, Sumant, Nyayadhish and Panditrao.

q.s: The first printing press in India was set up by the Portuguese at Goa in the year:
q.x: The Portuguese set up the first press at Goa in 1556.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT introduced into India by the Portuguese?
q.x: Rice is native to India; tobacco, potato and chilli came through the Portuguese.

q.s: On the eve of the Revolt of 1857, which region was called the 'nursery of the Bengal Army'?
q.x: Most Bengal Army sepoys came from Awadh, hence the name.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the army on the eve of 1857 is correct?
o: Indian sepoys outnumbered European soldiers by about five to one
The sepoys had no links with rural grievances
European troops had been drawn off for the Afghan wars
Most Bengal Army sepoys came from Punjab
q.x: Sepoys outnumbered Europeans about 5 to 1. European troops had gone to the Crimean and Persian wars, and the sepoys were 'peasants in uniform' from Awadh.

q.s: Who was the first to hold the title 'Viceroy and Governor-General' of India under the Government of India Act, 1858?
q.x: Canning, the last Company Governor-General, became the first Viceroy of the Crown.

q.s: Who founded the autonomous Nawabi of Bengal in the early 18th century?
q.x: Murshid Quli Khan founded the autonomous Bengal Nawabi.

q.s: Under the Bengal Nawabs, the ijaradari system meant collecting land revenue through:
q.x: Ijaradari (mal jasmani) meant revenue collection through contractors or revenue farmers.

q.s: The Gond rising at Jodeghat (1938-44) in the Hyderabad State was led by:
q.x: Komaram Bheem led the Gonds at Jodeghat under the slogan Jal, Jangal, Zameen.

q.s: Which of the following tribal leaders did NOT lead a rising in the Andhra or Hyderabad region?
q.x: Birsa Munda led the Munda Ulgulan in Chotanagpur; the others led risings in Andhra or Hyderabad.

q.s: The Censorship of Press Act, 1799 was passed by:
q.x: Wellesley passed the 1799 Act; John Adams issued the Licensing Regulations of 1823.

q.s: M.C. Rajah, a leader of the depressed classes of Madras, was associated with the:
q.x: M.C. Rajah led the All India Depressed Classes Association; the other three were Ambedkar's organisations.

q.s: Which of the following organisations was NOT founded by B.R. Ambedkar?
q.x: M.C. Rajah was associated with the All India Depressed Classes Association.

q.s: Sree Narayana Guru consecrated a Shiva idol in 1888 at:
q.x: The Aruvippuram consecration (1888) was a landmark of the Ezhava reform movement.

q.s: Ayyankali's Sadhu Jana Paripalana Sangham worked for the uplift of the:
q.x: Ayyankali worked among the Pulayas of Travancore; the SNDP Yogam worked among the Ezhavas.

q.s: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) was founded in 1949 by:
q.x: Annadurai broke from Periyar's Dravidar Kazhagam to form the DMK on 17 September 1949.

q.s: The Dravidar Kazhagam was formed in the year:
q.x: The Dravidar Kazhagam came in 1944, after the anti-Hindi agitation (1937) and the Dravidistan demand at Erode (1940).

q.s: The Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam (1883), written to oppose Veeresalingam's widow remarriage campaign, was authored by:
q.x: Vedam Venkataraya Sastri wrote it; Paidah Ramakrishnayya funded remarriages at Kakinada.

q.s: Pandita Ramabai's Sharada Sadan, a home for widows, was started in 1889 at:
q.x: Sharada Sadan began at Bombay in 1889; her Arya Mahila Samaj (1882) was at Pune.

q.s: India's first Women's University was founded in 1916 by:
q.x: Dhondo Keshav Karve founded it in 1916 and received the Bharat Ratna in 1958.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a leader of the Aligarh Movement?
q.x: Mahmud-ul-Hasan belonged to the Deoband school; the others led the later Aligarh Movement.

q.s: The Moderate campaign against the partition of Bengal in 1903-05 relied mainly on:
q.x: The Moderates used petitions, public meetings and the press; the Extremists took over from 1906 with passive resistance.

q.s: Who was the first president of the Ghadar Party, founded in the USA in 1913?
q.x: Sohan Singh Bhakna was the first president; Lala Har Dayal was its general secretary.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Lala Har Dayal is correct?
o: He founded the Indian Independence League at Tokyo
He was hanged in the Lahore Conspiracy Case
He belonged to the India House circle in London
He was the first president of the Ghadar Party
q.x: Har Dayal was in the India House circle and was the Ghadar general secretary, arrested in the USA in 1914.

q.s: Annie Besant became President of the Theosophical Society in the year:
q.x: She came to India in 1893, became President of the Theosophical Society in 1907 and President of the INC in 1917.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Annie Besant is correct?
o: She presided over the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1917
C.W. Leadbeater was the first principal of her National College, Madanapalle
She founded the Banaras Hindu University in 1916
Her protege Jiddu Krishnamurti wrote 'The Secret Doctrine'
q.x: Besant presided over the 1917 Calcutta Congress. BHU was founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya, J.H. Cousins headed Madanapalle, and The Secret Doctrine is Blavatsky's.

q.s: Pochampalli in Telangana is historically associated with the:
q.x: Vinoba Bhave received the first Bhoodan gift at Pochampalli in 1951.

q.s: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was led by:
q.x: Vallabhbhai Patel led the Bardoli no-tax campaign and earned the title Sardar.

q.s: At midnight on 31 December 1929 Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the tricolour on the banks of the Ravi at the Congress session held at:
q.x: The Lahore session (1929) adopted Purna Swaraj as the goal.

q.s: Lord Irwin's 'Deepavali Declaration' of 31 October 1929 named which of the following as the goal for India?
q.x: Irwin named Dominion Status as the goal but set no time-limit.

q.s: The Muzaffarpur bomb of Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki (1908) was aimed at:
q.x: It was aimed at the magistrate Kingsford; Rand was shot by the Chapekar brothers in 1897.

q.s: Babu Genu, a martyr of the Civil Disobedience Movement, was crushed by a lorry carrying foreign cloth in December 1930 at:
q.x: Babu Genu died in Bombay while blocking a lorry carrying foreign cloth.

q.s: The Communal Award of 1932 was announced by the British Prime Minister:
q.x: Ramsay MacDonald (PM 1929-35) announced the Communal Award in August 1932.

q.s: Who was the British Prime Minister when the Cabinet Mission came to India in 1946?
q.x: Attlee (1945-51) sent the Cabinet Mission and presided over Indian independence.

q.s: The Cripps Mission of 1942 was sent to India by the British Prime Minister:
q.x: Churchill sent Cripps, a member of his War Cabinet; Attlee became PM only in 1945.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Sir Stafford Cripps is correct?
o: He was a leader of the Conservative Party
He was a member of Churchill's War Cabinet
He was sent to India in 1942 by Prime Minister Attlee
He was not a member of the Cabinet Mission of 1946
q.x: Cripps, a Labour leader in Churchill's War Cabinet, came in 1942 and was later on the Cabinet Mission.

q.s: After his return from South Africa, Gandhi set up his first ashram in India in May 1915 at:
q.x: The Satyagraha Ashram was first at Kochrab, Ahmedabad (1915), and moved to Sabarmati in 1917.

q.s: Gandhi received the Kaisar-i-Hind gold medal in 1915 for his ambulance work in South Africa from:
q.x: Lord Hardinge (Viceroy 1910-16) conferred the medal in 1915.

q.s: The term 'Gandhian Innovation', meaning getting more from less for more people, was coined by:
q.x: C.K. Prahalad and R.A. Mashelkar coined 'Gandhian Innovation'.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Gandhian economic idea?
q.x: Gandhi wanted production for need (consumption), not for profit.

q.s: Operation Barga (1977), the most notable success of tenancy reform in India, was carried out in:
q.x: Operation Barga registered sharecroppers (bargadars) in West Bengal.

q.s: Consolidation of land holdings in India was successful in all of the following EXCEPT:
q.x: Consolidation succeeded mainly in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

q.s: Who became the first Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly after the merger of 1956?
q.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker of AP; Kashinatha Rao Vaidya was Speaker of Hyderabad State.

q.s: Gautamiputra Satakarni is described as 'Ekabrahmana' in the:
q.x: The Nasik inscription of his mother Gautami Balasri calls him Ekabrahmana.

q.s: The Malkapuram inscription of 1261 CE belongs to the reign of:
q.x: The Malkapuram inscription (1261) was issued in Rudramadevi's reign and mentions the instrument Jalakaranda.

q.s: Gupta stone sculpture is regarded as a continuation of which school of art?
q.x: Gupta sculpture grew out of the indigenous Mathura tradition.

q.s: The Gupta-age Sarnath school of sculpture mainly used:
q.x: Sarnath used Chunar sandstone; Mathura used spotted red sandstone and Gandhara blue-grey schist.

q.s: A Buddhist stupa that contained no relics and was purely commemorative is called:
q.x: Uddeshika stupas were commemorative; Dhatugarbha stupas held bodily relics and Paribhogika stupas objects used by the Buddha or monks.

q.s: After the Nagarjunakonda valley was submerged by the Nagarjuna Sagar project, the ASI rebuilt its monuments at:
q.x: The monuments were rebuilt at Anupu on the Krishna and on the island museum.

q.s: India's only island museum is located at:
q.x: The island museum is on Nagarjunakonda in the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir.

q.s: The Archaeological Survey of India was set up in 1861 with which of the following as its first head?
q.x: Alexander Cunningham founded and first headed the ASI (1861).

q.s: The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act was passed in:
q.x: The AMASR Act is of 1958; the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act is of 1972.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of society in the Vishnukundin period?
q.x: In the Vishnukundin period varna rules hardened and the status of women declined.

q.s: Brick structural temples of the Vishnukundin period, with garbhagriha, antarala-mandapa and mukhamandapa, are found at:
q.x: Keesaragutta has Vishnukundin brick temples; Undavalli and Mogalrajapuram are cave temples.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Vishnukundin art is correct?
o: Keesaragutta has only rock-cut caves and no structural temples
The Undavalli caves were excavated by the Kakatiyas
Early multi-armed metal images made by the lost-wax method are credited to the Vishnukundin age
Their cave temples are dated to the 10th century CE
q.x: Lost-wax multi-armed images are Vishnukundin. Their caves are of the 4th-6th centuries, and Keesaragutta has brick structural temples.

q.s: The Kailasa temple (Cave 16) at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta king:
q.x: Krishna I built the rock-cut Kailasa temple in the Dravida style.

q.s: The northern campaign of the Rashtrakuta king Govinda III up to the Himalayas is described in the:
q.x: The Sanjan plates describe Govinda III's Himalayan campaign; the Aihole inscription is of Pulakesin II.

q.s: Which Badami Chalukya ruler, regarded as the real founder of the dynasty, performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice?
q.x: Pulakesin I performed the Ashvamedha; Vikramaditya I later revived Chalukya power after the Pallava occupation of Vatapi.

q.s: The earliest rock-cut caves at Badami were excavated in the reign of:
q.x: The early Badami caves belong to Mangalesha's reign.

q.s: The Dayabhaga, a treatise on Hindu law of inheritance, was written by:
q.x: Jimutavahana of Bengal wrote the Dayabhaga; Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara.

q.s: The Dayabhaga school of Hindu law prevails mainly in:
q.x: Dayabhaga prevails in Bengal and Assam; the Mitakshara in most of India.

q.s: During the Reddi period, the form of religion patronised by the Reddi kings was:
q.x: The Reddi kings, disciples of the Ghoderayas, patronised Pashupata Shaivism; Veerashaivism was the popular religion.

q.s: Which of the following statements about religion in the Reddi period is correct?
o: The Ghoderayas spread Shaivism from Tripurantakam
The Reddi kings were patrons of Jainism
The Vadagalai matha of the period was at Srisailam
q.x: The Ghoderayas, gurus of the Reddi kings, worked from Tripurantakam. The Vadagalai matha was at Ahobilam, and Veerashaivism was the popular religion.

q.s: The Raichur Doab, the chief bone of contention between the Bahmanis and Vijayanagara, lay between the rivers:
q.x: The Raichur Doab is the land between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra.

q.s: Bidriware, a blackened zinc alloy inlaid with silver, developed under the Bahmani rulers at:
q.x: Bidriware takes its name from Bidar, the later Bahmani capital.

q.s: The first usurpation in the Vijayanagara empire (1485), which ended the Sangama dynasty, was carried out by:
q.x: Saluva Narasimha expelled Praudhadeva Raya, the last Sangama, in 1485.

q.s: Krishnadevaraya of the Tuluva dynasty was crowned in the year:
q.x: He was crowned on 8 August 1509 and ruled until 1529.

q.s: Krishnadevaraya's titles 'Andhra Bhoja' and 'Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma' reflect his:
q.x: Both titles honour his scholarship and patronage of literature.

q.s: Krishnadevaraya named Nagalapuram, a suburb of Vijayanagara, after his:
q.x: Nagalapuram honours his mother Nagala Devi; Hospet (Tirumaladevipattana) honours his queen Tirumaladevi.

q.s: The three trilingual Sadasivakona inscriptions of the Vijayanagara period, reported by the ASI in June 2026, were found in the Seshachalam forest of:
q.x: They were found in the Seshachalam forest of Tirupati district and are dated 1554 CE.

q.s: In the Vijayanagara Ayagar system, the village officer who kept the accounts and the land and crop registers was the:
q.x: The Karanam kept accounts; the Reddi was village head, the Talari the watchman and the Begari supervised forced labour.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the village officers (Ayagars) under Vijayanagara?
q.x: The Amaranayaka was a military chief holding an amaram; the Ayagars were village servants such as Karanam, Reddi and Talari.

q.s: The Vilasa copper-plate grant (1330), describing the sufferings of the Andhra country under Tughlaq rule, was issued by:
q.x: Prolaya Nayaka issued the Vilasa grant, which also records restoring agraharas to Brahmins.

q.s: Narahari Tirtha spread which philosophy from Srikurmam in the Andhra country?
q.x: Narahari Tirtha, a disciple of Madhva, spread Dvaita from Srikurmam.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Shaiva centre of Andhra?
q.x: Ahobilam is famous for its Narasimha temples; the others are Shaiva centres.

q.s: The Thousand Pillar temple at Hanumakonda, built by the Kakatiyas, is dedicated to:
q.x: Its deities are Rudreswara (Shiva), Vasudeva (Vishnu) and Surya; Surya takes Brahma's place.

q.s: The monolithic Nandi of the Thousand Pillar temple at Hanumakonda is carved out of:
q.x: The Nandi is a black basalt monolith; the temple actually has 369 pillars.

q.s: The Naga linga at Lepakshi is sheltered by a serpent, carved from the same boulder, with how many hoods?
q.x: The Lepakshi Naga linga has a seven-hooded serpent.

q.s: The nationalist paper Krishna Patrika was associated with:
q.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited Krishna Patrika.

q.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao, one of the first political prisoners of Andhra, edited the journal:
q.x: Gadicherla edited Swarajya (1908) and was jailed for it; Desamata is linked with Chilakamarti.

q.s: The Bala Bharati Samiti of the Vandemataram movement was founded in February 1907 at:
q.x: Local youths such as Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao founded it at Rajahmundry.

q.s: The all-India ban on the Communist Party of India, imposed in 1934, was lifted in the year:
q.x: The ban ran from 23 July 1934 to 23 July 1942; the Andhra ban of 1949 was lifted in 1951.

q.s: After the communist paper Prajasakti was banned in 1948, which paper took its place in 1952?
q.x: Visalandhra replaced Prajasakti in 1952.

q.s: Which Telugu poet of the Bhava Kavitvam school is known as 'Andhra Shelley'?
q.x: Devulapalli Krishna Sastri is called Andhra Shelley.

q.s: Which of the following poets did NOT belong to the Bhava Kavitvam (romantic) school?
q.x: Sri Sri led the Abhyudaya (progressive) movement; Rayaprolu wrote Andhravali.

q.s: The Viplava Rachayitala Sangham (Virasam), the revolutionary writers' body of Andhra, was formed in:
q.x: Virasam was formed in 1970, carrying Telugu poetry towards class struggle.

q.s: Which Telugu writers' organisation of the 1930s-40s was associated with Abhyudaya (progressive) literature?
q.x: Arasam (Abhyudaya Rachayitala Sangham) led progressive literature before Virasam.

q.s: Sati Hitabodhini (1883), the first Telugu journal for women, was started by:
q.x: Veeresalingam started Sati Hitabodhini in 1883; Rayasam Venkata Sivudu ran Zenana Patrika (1894).

q.s: The Dhimsa dance, performed by tribal women of the Visakhapatnam agency in circles with hands on one another's shoulders, traces its origin to:
q.x: Dhimsa originated in Koraput (Odisha).

q.s: The first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission (1968-70) was headed by:
q.x: The Anantharaman Commission grouped the BCs into A-D; Mandal and Kalelkar headed national commissions.

q.s: Puttumacha ('Birthmark'), a long Telugu poem on Muslim identity, was written by:
q.x: Khadar Mohiuddin wrote Puttumacha; Jaljala (1990s) is an anthology of Muslim minority poetry.

q.s: The Telugu feminist poetry anthology 'Neeli Meghalu' was published in:
q.x: Neeli Meghalu appeared in 1993.

q.s: Bhakta Prahlada (1931), the first Telugu talkie, was directed by:
q.x: H.M. Reddy directed Bhakta Prahlada; Bhishma Pratigna (1921) was the first Telugu silent film.

q.s: Which was the first full-length Telugu colour film (1963)?
q.x: Lava Kusa (1963) was the first full-length Telugu colour film.

q.s: Annapurna Studios in Hyderabad was founded by:
q.x: ANR founded Annapurna Studios; Ramoji Rao founded Ramoji Film City and B. Nagi Reddy and Chakrapani Vijaya Vauhini.

q.s: The children's magazine Chandamama was started at Madras in July 1947 by:
o: K.V. Reddy and Pingali Nagendra Rao
q.x: B. Nagi Reddy and Aluri Chakrapani started Chandamama in 1947.

q.s: At present, the National Film Awards of India are administered by the:
q.x: The NFDC now runs the National Film Awards, which were formerly handled by the Directorate of Film Festivals.

q.s: In sociology, the process by which a minority group is absorbed into the dominant culture and loses its own identity is called:
q.x: Assimilation absorbs the minority; in acculturation both cultures change but remain distinct.

q.s: The blending of global and local cultural elements under globalisation is called:
q.x: Hybridisation is the blend of global and local; diffusion is the spread of traits from one society to another.

q.s: The idea of 'seed sovereignty' and the critique of biopiracy are associated with:
q.x: Vandana Shiva champions seed sovereignty; Stiglitz is known for critiquing IMF policy conditions.

q.s: In G.P. Murdock's scheme of the functions of the family, the birth of children is the:
q.x: Murdock's four functions are sexual, reproductive, economic and educational; birth of children is the reproductive function.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of G.P. Murdock's four universal functions of the family?
q.x: Murdock's four functions are sexual, reproductive, economic and educational.

q.s: The distinction between classificatory and descriptive kinship terminology was proposed in 1871 by:
q.x: Morgan proposed it in 'Systems of Consanguinity and Affinity' (1871).

q.s: Using a single kinship term such as 'uncle' for several different relatives is an example of:
q.x: One term for several relatives is classificatory; descriptive terms name a single relation.

q.s: M.N. Srinivas developed the concept of 'dominant caste' from his study of the village of:
q.x: Srinivas studied Rampura near Mysore; Shamirpet was studied by S.C. Dube and Kishan Garhi by McKim Marriott.

q.s: India signed CEDAW in 1980 and ratified it in the year:
q.x: India ratified CEDAW in 1993, with a reservation on Article 29(1).

q.s: The Family Courts Act was enacted in:
q.x: The Family Courts Act is of 1984; Family Courts are set up by State Governments in consultation with the High Court.

q.s: India's first exclusive women's court was set up in 2013 at:
q.x: The first women's court was set up at Malda, West Bengal.

q.s: The implementation of the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 is monitored by the:
q.x: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis monitors the Act.

q.s: B.R. Ambedkar declared in 1935, 'I was born a Hindu, but I will not die a Hindu', at:
q.x: The Yeola declaration was made in 1935; the conversion took place at Nagpur in 1956.

q.s: The Srikrishna Committee (2010) was constituted to examine the:
o: Site of the new capital of Andhra Pradesh
Demand for a separate Telangana State
q.x: The Srikrishna Committee studied the Telangana/united AP question and gave six options; the Bhargava Committee dealt with surplus funds.

q.s: The expert committee that studied the location of the new capital of Andhra Pradesh under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 was headed by:
q.x: The Sivaramakrishnan Committee (2014) studied the capital site.

q.s: According to the NCRB's Crime in India 2024, the State with the highest violent-crime rate was:
q.x: Odisha had the highest violent-crime rate in the 2024 report.

q.s: Crime in India 2024 is the first NCRB report to present data under the:
q.x: It is the first report with data under the BNS, which replaced the IPC.

q.s: The National Youth Policy 2014 defines 'youth' as persons in the age group of:
q.x: NYP 2014 covers 15-29 years; NYP 2003 covered 13-35 years.

q.s: India's first National Youth Policy was adopted in:
q.x: The first National Youth Policy came in 1988.

q.s: The first poverty-line study in India (1971), using a norm of 2,250 calories, was made by:
q.x: Dandekar and Rath made the first study; Hashim (2009) dealt with urban BPL and Saxena (2009) with the rural BPL census.

q.s: The Alagh Task Force (1979) based the poverty line on a daily calorie need of:
q.x: Alagh fixed 2,400 calories for rural and 2,100 for urban areas.

q.s: Under G.O. 43 of June 2024, the Andhra Pradesh old-age pension was raised from Rs 3,000 to:
q.x: The NTR Bharosa old-age pension was raised to Rs 4,000 a month.

q.s: The NTR Bharosa Pension scheme of Andhra Pradesh was earlier called:
q.x: It was earlier the YSR Pension Kanuka; Aasara is Telangana's pension scheme.

q.s: Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, the maximum maintenance allowance is:
q.x: The cap is Rs 10,000 a month, and a case is to be decided within 90 days.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Senior Citizens Act, 2007 is correct?
o: Its medical care programme, the NPHCE, is run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
A maintenance case must be decided within 30 days
A property transfer made on condition of care can be declared void if the transferee neglects the parent
In Andhra Pradesh the Maintenance Tribunal is headed by the District Collector
q.x: Section 23 allows such transfers to be declared void. The NPHCE is under the Health Ministry, and the AP Tribunal is headed by the RDO/Sub-Collector.

q.s: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), launched on 15 August 1995, is administered by the Ministry of:
q.x: NSAP is under the Ministry of Rural Development.

q.s: Under the Annapurna scheme of the NSAP, eligible senior citizens not receiving IGNOAPS get free food grains of:
q.x: Annapurna gives 10 kg of food grains a month to seniors not covered by IGNOAPS.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court recognise transgender persons as the 'third gender' in 2014?
o: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
q.x: NALSA (2014) recognised the third gender; Puttaswamy (2017) made privacy a fundamental right.

q.s: Consensual same-sex relations were decriminalised under Section 377 IPC by the Supreme Court in:
o: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
Suresh Kumar Koushal v. Naz Foundation
q.x: Navtej Singh Johar (2018) decriminalised them; Koushal (2013) had restored Section 377.

q.s: The MY Bharat (Mera Yuva Bharat) platform comes under the Ministry of:
q.x: MY Bharat is under Youth Affairs and Sports; the Skill India Digital Hub is under MSDE.

q.s: The PM-DevINE scheme is implemented by the Ministry of:
q.x: PM-DevINE is a DoNER scheme for the North East.

q.s: 'Yudh Abhyas' is a joint military exercise between India and the USA of their:
q.x: Yudh Abhyas is an army exercise; Red Flag is a US Air Force exercise.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an India-USA bilateral military exercise?
q.x: Garuda is an India-France air exercise; Tiger Triumph is India-US tri-service.

q.s: The post-Hudhud Andhra Pradesh Disaster Recovery Project is funded by the:
q.x: The World Bank funds the post-Hudhud recovery project.

q.s: For Phase I of the Amaravati capital, the World Bank and the ADB each committed:
q.x: Each committed $800 million; the IBRD gave $1.5 billion for the Green Hydrogen Mission.

q.s: The IBSA Dialogue Forum of India, Brazil and South Africa was founded in 2003 through the:
q.x: IBSA was set up by the Brasilia Declaration of June 2003.

q.s: IBSAMAR, associated with the IBSA grouping, is a:
q.x: IBSAMAR is the IBSA naval exercise; the IBSA Trust Fund is run by UNOSSC.

q.s: Article 338B of the Constitution deals with the:
q.x: Art. 338B (102nd Amendment) is the NCBC; 338 is NCSC, 338A NCST and 280 the Finance Commission.

q.s: At present, the right to property in India is a:
q.x: The 44th Amendment removed it from Part III; it is now a constitutional (legal) right under Article 300A.

q.s: In Dr Balram Singh v. Union of India (2024), the Supreme Court upheld the insertion in the Preamble of the words:
q.x: On 25 November 2024 the Court upheld 'Socialist' and 'Secular', added by the 42nd Amendment.

q.s: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution has so far been amended only once, by the:
q.x: The 42nd Amendment added Socialist, Secular and Integrity.

q.s: Under which Article does the President appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes?
q.x: Art. 340 provides for such a commission (e.g. the Mandal Commission).

q.s: The National Commission for Backward Classes was given constitutional status by the:
q.x: The 102nd Amendment (2018) inserted Article 338B.

q.s: Which clause of Article 19 allows the State to prescribe professional or technical qualifications for practising a profession?
q.x: Art. 19(6) covers restrictions on profession, trade and business, including State monopoly.

q.s: Which of the following freedoms is NO longer guaranteed under Article 19?
o: Freedom to move freely throughout India
Right to acquire, hold and dispose of property
q.x: Article 19(1)(f) on property was deleted by the 44th Amendment (1978).

q.s: In which case was judicial review under Articles 226 and 227 held to be part of the basic structure?
q.x: L. Chandra Kumar (1997) held so; Kesavananda Bharati laid down the basic structure doctrine.

q.s: The maxim 'a right without a remedy is a worthless declaration' explains the importance of:
q.x: Art. 32, the right to constitutional remedies, makes the other rights enforceable.

q.s: The doctrine of colourable legislation is associated with the case:
o: K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa
Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v. State of M.P.
M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum gas)
q.x: Gajapati Narayan Deo (1953): colourable legislation; Bhikaji Narain: eclipse; Kamal Nath: public trust; Oleum gas: absolute liability.

q.s: The doctrine of absolute liability was laid down by the Supreme Court in the:
q.x: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987), the Oleum gas case, laid down absolute liability.

q.s: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution (right to life and personal liberty) corresponds to which Article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
q.x: UDHR Art. 3 is life and liberty; Art. 7 equality before law, Art. 8 remedies, Art. 26 education.

q.s: Education was moved from the State List to the Concurrent List by the:
q.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) moved education to the Concurrent List; the 86th inserted Article 21A.

q.s: Repugnancy between a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject is dealt with in:
q.x: Under Art. 254 the Union law prevails and the State law is void to the extent of repugnancy.

q.s: As of November 2026, the latest enacted amendment to the Constitution of India is the:
q.x: The 106th Amendment (2023) provided for women's reservation in legislatures.

q.s: Who said that the Indian amending procedure 'appears complicated but is merely diverse'?
q.x: Granville Austin said so; K.C. Wheare praised its balance of rigidity and flexibility.

q.s: The veto under which the President of India may return a non-money Bill for reconsideration, but must assent if it is passed again, is called:
q.x: This is the suspensive veto.

q.s: Which of the following vetoes is NOT available to the President of India?
q.x: The Indian President has absolute, suspensive and pocket vetoes; the qualified veto (overridable by a higher majority) belongs to the US President.

q.s: The present maximum strength of the Lok Sabha as provided in Article 81 is:
q.x: The maximum is 550; 552 included two nominated Anglo-Indians until January 2020, and the present strength is 543.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court uphold the open ballot and the removal of the domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha elections?
o: Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India
Lily Thomas v. Union of India
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
q.x: Kuldip Nayar (2006) upheld both changes.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a qualification for a candidate to Parliament?
o: Being an elector in a parliamentary constituency
q.x: No educational qualification is prescribed for membership of Parliament.

q.s: Under the Constitution, the gap between the last sitting of one session of Parliament and the first sitting of the next cannot exceed:
q.x: Art. 85 lays down the six-month rule; the three sessions are a convention.

q.s: Which session of Parliament is usually the longest?
q.x: The Budget session is the longest and the Winter session the shortest.

q.s: Under which Article does the President make a special address to Parliament at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year?
q.x: Art. 87 provides for the special address; Art. 86 lets the President address or send messages to the Houses.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the President's special address to Parliament is correct?
o: It is prepared by the Government and sets out its policy
It is made at the beginning of every session
It is prepared by the President's own Secretariat
q.x: The address is the Government's policy statement, made under Article 87 at the first session after an election and the first session of each year.

q.s: The defeat of the Motion of Thanks on the President's address in the Lok Sabha amounts to:
q.x: The address is the Government's policy statement, so its rejection is a defeat of the Government.

q.s: The passage of a cut motion in the Lok Sabha is treated as:
o: Loss of confidence in the Government
q.x: Under collective responsibility, losing a cut motion means the Government has lost the House's support.

q.s: A cut motion that seeks to reduce a demand to Re 1, expressing disapproval of a policy, is called a:
q.x: Policy cut: Re 1; economy cut: a specified amount; token cut: Rs 100.

q.s: Who among the following was the first President of India to die in office?
q.x: Zakir Husain died in office in May 1969.

q.s: Which President of India was elected in 1969 on the counting of second-preference votes?
q.x: V.V. Giri won the 1969 election on second-preference votes.

q.s: Which President of India used the pocket veto on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill, 1986?
q.x: Zail Singh kept the Post Office Bill pending (pocket veto); Venkataraman used the absolute veto on the 1991 MPs' salary Bill.

q.s: The word 'Cabinet' appears in the Constitution only in Article 352(3), which was inserted by the:
q.x: The 44th Amendment required the Cabinet's written advice for a National Emergency.

q.s: The collective responsibility of the Union Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha is laid down in:
q.x: Art. 75(3) is collective responsibility; 75(2) is individual responsibility (President's pleasure).

q.s: Under which Article of the Constitution does the Governor assent to, withhold assent from, or reserve a State Bill for the President?
q.x: Art. 200 deals with the Governor's options on Bills; Art. 201 with Bills reserved for the President.

q.s: In State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor (April 2025), the Supreme Court declared ten re-enacted Bills as deemed assented using its powers under:
q.x: The Court used Art. 142; the November 2025 Presidential Reference opinion later rejected deemed assent.

q.s: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 limits the size of a State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, to:
o: 15 per cent of the Assembly's total strength
20 per cent of the Assembly's total strength
12 per cent of the Assembly's total strength
10 per cent of the Assembly's total strength
q.x: Art. 164(1A): at most 15 per cent and at least 12 Ministers.

q.s: With 175 Assembly seats, the maximum number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, that Andhra Pradesh can have is:
q.x: 15 per cent of 175 is 26.25, so the limit is 26.

q.s: The Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed by the President after consulting the:
o: Union Law Minister and the Governor
Prime Minister and the Chief Justice of India
Chief Minister and the Governor of the State
Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the State
q.x: Art. 217: the President consults the CJI and the Governor; proposals start with the High Court collegium.

q.s: Unlike a Supreme Court judge, a High Court judge cannot be appointed from among:
o: Advocates of two or more High Courts in succession
Advocates of a High Court of ten years' standing
Holders of judicial office for ten years
q.x: Only a Supreme Court judge may be a distinguished jurist in the President's opinion.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution declares the Directive Principles of State Policy non-justiciable?
q.x: Art. 37 says the DPSPs are not enforceable by any court but are fundamental in governance.

q.s: Which of the following statements about quasi-judicial bodies in India is correct?
o: Their decisions are final and cannot be appealed
They form part of the regular hierarchy of courts
They are strictly bound by the Code of Civil Procedure
They must follow the principles of natural justice
q.x: Quasi-judicial bodies are not bound by the CPC but must follow natural justice, and their decisions are appealable.

q.s: The federal scheme of the Indian Constitution was mainly drawn from the:
q.x: The federal scheme came largely from the Government of India Act, 1935.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Governor of a State is appointed by the President under Article 155
Officers of the All India Services are recruited through the State PSCs
Ratification of a federal amendment needs a special majority in each State Legislature
The Governor of a State is appointed under Article 163
q.x: Arts 155-156 deal with the Governor's appointment; Art. 163 is the State Council of Ministers, AIS officers come through the UPSC, and State ratification needs only a simple majority.

q.s: 'The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation' was written by:
q.x: The book is Granville Austin's; Alexandrowicz called India 'a case sui generis'.

q.s: Who described the Indian Constitution as 'a case sui generis'?
q.x: Alexandrowicz used 'sui generis'; Wheare called India 'quasi-federal'.

q.s: A State Bill imposing reasonable restrictions on inter-State trade in the public interest requires the President's previous sanction under:
q.x: Art. 304(b) needs the President's previous sanction; Art. 301 declares freedom of trade.

q.s: Under which Article can Parliament legislate on a State List subject when the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution in the national interest?
q.x: Art. 249: Rajya Sabha resolution by two-thirds; Art. 252: two or more States' resolutions; Art. 253: treaties.

q.s: Parliament can make laws on a State List subject in all of the following situations EXCEPT:
o: On the recommendation of the Finance Commission
A resolution of the Rajya Sabha in the national interest
Resolutions of two or more State Legislatures
q.x: Arts 249, 252, 253 and 356/357 allow it; the Finance Commission has no such role.

q.s: In the GST Council, the vote of the Union Government carries a weight of:
q.x: The Centre has one-third, the States together two-thirds, and decisions need a three-fourths majority.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the GST Council is correct?
o: Each member, Union or State, has an equal vote
In Mohit Minerals (2022) its recommendations were held binding on legislatures
Its members are the Union Finance Minister, the Union MoS for Revenue/Finance and every State's Finance Minister
Its decisions need a simple majority of members present
q.x: Votes are weighted (Centre one-third), decisions need three-fourths, and Mohit Minerals held the recommendations persuasive.

q.s: The annual report of a State Public Service Commission is submitted to the:
q.x: SPSC reports go to the Governor; the UPSC report goes to the President.

q.s: Every case of non-acceptance of the UPSC's advice by the Union Government needs the approval of the:
q.x: Non-acceptance of UPSC advice must be approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.

q.s: The First Backward Classes Commission, set up in 1953, was headed by:
q.x: Kaka Kalelkar headed the first commission (1953); B.P. Mandal the second (1979).

q.s: Reservation for backward communities was first introduced in 1902 in Kolhapur by:
q.x: Shahu Maharaj of Kolhapur reserved posts for backward classes in 1902.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment restored the power of the States to prepare their own lists of socially and educationally backward classes?
q.x: The 105th Amendment restored the States' lists after the Maratha reservation judgment.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the backward classes provisions is correct?
o: The 102nd Amendment inserted Article 342A on notifying socially and educationally backward classes
The NCBC is provided for in Article 338
The 105th Amendment took away the States' power to keep their own SEBC lists
The 102nd Amendment added backward classes work to the National Commission for SCs
q.x: The 102nd inserted Arts 338B and 342A and relieved the NCSC of BC work; the 105th restored the States' lists.

q.s: Civil Services Day is observed in India every year on:
q.x: It marks Patel's address to the first probationers on 21 April 1947; DARPG has organised it since 2006.

q.s: Who called the civil services the 'steel frame of India' while addressing probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi, in 1947?
q.x: Sardar Patel used the phrase on 21 April 1947.

q.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India holds office for:
o: Six years or up to 65 years of age
Five years or up to 60 years of age
Five years or up to 65 years of age
Six years or up to 62 years of age
q.x: The CAG's term is six years or till 65, whichever is earlier.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
q.x: The NHRC is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; the NCBC became constitutional in 2018.

q.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women (1992-95)?
q.x: Jayanti Patnaik was the first NCW chair; Vijaya Rahatkar has headed it since October 2024.

q.s: Who has been the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women since October 2024?
q.x: Vijaya Rahatkar succeeded Rekha Sharma (2018-24).

q.s: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, the Central Information Commission is constituted under:
q.x: Section 12: CIC; 15: State ICs; 11: third-party information; 25: annual report.

q.s: Financial relations between the Union and the States are dealt with in which Part of the Constitution?
q.x: Part XII covers finance; Part XI covers legislative and administrative relations.

q.s: The 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council, held on 20 August 2026, took place in:
q.x: The 31st meeting was in Tamil Nadu; the 29th was at Tirupati.

q.s: The Zonal Councils, set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, are chaired by the:
q.x: The Union Home Minister chairs each Zonal Council.

q.s: The Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog is appointed by the:
q.x: The PM, as Chairperson, appoints the Vice-Chairperson.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog?
q.x: The Governing Council has the PM, CMs (including Delhi, J&K and Puducherry) and LGs of other UTs; it took over the role of the NDC.

q.s: The Rajamannar Committee (1969) on Centre-State relations was appointed by the Government of:
q.x: The DMK government of Tamil Nadu appointed it in 1969.

q.s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended that the residuary powers be vested in the:
q.x: It wanted residuary powers given to the States and found they had become 'administrative units of the Centre'.

q.s: The recognition of political parties and the allotment of election symbols in India are governed by the:
q.x: Recognition rests on the ECI's Symbols Order, 1968, based on poll performance.

q.s: Registration of political parties with the Election Commission is provided for under:
q.x: Section 29A of the RPA 1951 deals with registration; Para 6B of the Symbols Order lays down national-party criteria.

q.s: The main own source of revenue of Urban Local Bodies in India is:
q.x: Property tax is the main own revenue of ULBs, though it is under-assessed and under-collected.

q.s: The 16th Finance Commission raised the urban share of local-body grants from 36 per cent to:
q.x: The urban share rose to 45 per cent, split 80 per cent basic and 20 per cent performance.

q.s: The Devolution Index 2024, ranking States on devolution to panchayats, was prepared by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj with:
q.x: The Indian Institute of Public Administration prepared it; it covers six dimensions, not finances alone.

q.s: The District Planning Committee, which consolidates the plans of panchayats and municipalities, was provided for by the:
q.x: The 74th Amendment inserted Art. 243ZD (DPC) and 243ZE (MPC).

q.s: The draft development plan prepared by the District Planning Committee is forwarded to the State Government by the:
q.x: The DPC chairperson sends the draft plan to the State Government.

q.s: Which industrial policy is called the 'economic constitution of India'?

q.s: District Industries Centres were introduced by the:
q.x: The Janata government's 1977 policy set up DICs.

q.s: Under Article 262(2), the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts over inter-State river water disputes may be barred by:
q.x: Parliament may bar the courts by law; it did so in Section 11 of the ISRWD Act, 1956.

q.s: The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act was enacted in:
q.x: The ISRWD Act, 1956 was enacted under Article 262.

q.s: Bhogapuram international airport in Andhra Pradesh is being developed under PPP by:
q.x: GMR is developing Bhogapuram on a DBFOT basis with a 3,800 m runway.

q.s: Orvakal airport (2021), the first State-built airport in South India, serves the city of:
q.x: Orvakal airport is near Kurnool; Kadapa is a domestic airport.

q.s: The WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement was concluded at the Ministerial Conference held at:
q.x: MC9 at Bali produced the Bali Package with the TFA and an interim Peace Clause on food stocks.

q.s: On the 2011 Census base, the urban share of the population of residuary Andhra Pradesh is about:
q.x: Residuary AP is about 29.6 per cent urban; India's figure was 31.1 per cent.

q.s: The National Rural Livelihoods Mission (2011) was modelled on Andhra Pradesh's:
q.x: Velugu's federated SHG model was adopted for NRLM; Kudumbashree is Kerala's and Jeevika Bihar's.

q.s: The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 is administered by the:
q.x: The EPFO runs the EPF; the ESIC runs the ESI scheme.

q.s: Since 2017, the wage ceiling for coverage under the ESI scheme is:
q.x: The ESI wage ceiling is Rs 21,000 a month.

q.s: Under the Public Distribution System in Andhra Pradesh, an Antyodaya Anna Yojana household gets rice of:

q.s: The investment multiplier (k) is given by:
The accelerator principle relating induced investment to a change in income is associated with:
q.x: J.M. Clark developed the accelerator; Kahn gave the employment multiplier.

q.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 was prepared under the Chief Economic Adviser:
q.x: V. Anantha Nageswaran is the CEA.

q.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 projected India's real GDP growth for FY27 at:
q.x: It projected 6.8-7.2 per cent and called FY27 a 'year of adjustment'.

q.s: Which institutional sector is the largest contributor to India's Gross Value Added?
q.x: The largely unorganised household sector is the largest; the private corporate share was 35.9 per cent in 2014-15.

q.s: As per Census 2011, which State had the highest share of cultivators among its workers?
q.x: Himachal Pradesh had 57.9 per cent cultivators among workers.

q.s: As per Census 2011, which State had the highest share of agricultural labourers among its workers?
q.x: Bihar had 52.8 per cent agricultural labourers.

q.s: Which committee of 1973 reviewed unemployment estimates and employment-oriented policies in India?
q.x: The Bhagwati Committee (1973) did so; the Dantwala Committee (1970) had rejected a single unemployment figure.

q.s: All of the following are indirect (fiscal) measures for reducing economic inequality EXCEPT:
q.x: Land ceilings redistribute assets directly; taxes act indirectly.

q.s: A fresh graduate who is searching for a first job is an example of:
q.x: Frictional unemployment is the time spent between or looking for jobs.

q.s: Lay-offs caused by a fall in aggregate demand during a recession are an example of:
q.x: Cyclical unemployment follows the business cycle; structural unemployment comes from long-run mismatch of skills or technology.

q.s: The main criticism of the Mahalanobis strategy of the Second Five Year Plan is that it:
q.x: Its stress on heavy industry and neglect of agriculture led to food and capital shortages and inflation in the late 1950s.

q.s: Which of the following steel plants was NOT set up during the Second Five Year Plan?
q.x: Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela came in the Second Plan; Bokaro came later.

q.s: Against a target of 4.5 per cent, the Second Five Year Plan achieved a growth rate of about:
q.x: The Second Plan achieved 4.27 per cent.

q.s: The idea of economic planning in India was mainly derived from the:
q.x: Indian planning was inspired by the Soviet five-year plans.

q.s: 'India: Planning for Industrialization' (1970), a critique of Indian planning, was co-authored by Jagdish Bhagwati and:
q.x: Bhagwati and Padma Desai wrote it; Desai's PhD was from Harvard.

q.s: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 merged how many central labour laws?
q.x: It merged the Trade Unions Act 1926, Standing Orders Act 1946 and Industrial Disputes Act 1947.

q.s: The four Labour Codes together subsumed how many central labour laws?
q.x: Wages 4 + Industrial Relations 3 + Social Security 9 + OSH 13 = 29 laws.

q.s: The Goods and Services Tax came into force in India on:
q.x: GST came through the 101st Amendment (2016) and began on 1 July 2017.

q.s: Which was the first State to ratify the GST Constitutional Amendment Bill?
q.x: Assam ratified first; Bihar was second.

q.s: The Thirteenth Finance Commission was chaired by:
q.x: Kelkar chaired the 13th, Y.V. Reddy the 14th, N.K. Singh the 15th and Arvind Panagariya the 16th.

q.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission is chaired by:
q.x: Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th FC; Annie George Mathew is a member.

q.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission, disaster funding for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States is shared between the Centre and the States in the ratio:
q.x: NE and Himalayan States share 90:10; other States 75:25.

q.s: Which type of grant to States did the Sixteenth Finance Commission discontinue?
q.x: The 16th FC ended revenue-deficit grants; local bodies get about Rs 7.91 lakh crore.

q.s: The minimum amount for a transaction through RTGS is:
q.x: RTGS has a Rs 2 lakh minimum; NEFT has none.

q.s: NEFT settles fund transfers on a:
q.x: NEFT settles in half-hourly batches on a deferred net basis; RTGS is real-time gross.

q.s: Bharat BillPay, operated by NPCI, is:
o: A system for bulk recurring payments
q.x: Bharat BillPay is for interoperable bill payments; NACH handles bulk recurring payments and BHIM is a UPI app.

q.s: Which of the following payment systems is NOT operated by NPCI?
q.x: RTGS is owned and operated by the RBI.

q.s: Chit fund companies in India are regulated by the:
q.x: Chit funds are regulated by State Governments under the Chit Funds Act, 1982.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT regulated by the Reserve Bank of India?
q.x: Insurance companies are regulated by IRDAI.

q.s: Which of the following is classified as developmental expenditure?
q.x: Irrigation is developmental; defence (including border roads), pensions and interest are non-developmental.

q.s: The Expenditure Management Commission (2014) was headed by:
q.x: Bimal Jalan headed it; Geethakrishnan headed the Expenditure Reforms Commission (2000).

q.s: Who was the first President of the BRICS New Development Bank (2015)?
q.x: K.V. Kamath was the first NDB President.

q.s: India's GST follows the dual-GST model of:
q.x: India's dual GST, levied by both Centre and States, follows the Canadian model.

q.s: The concept of GST was first introduced in:
q.x: France introduced GST first, in 1954.

q.s: Which of the following is a major item of India's exports to China?
q.x: India exports iron ore to China and imports electronics, solar cells and APIs from it.

q.s: The Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) is the Nominal Effective Exchange Rate adjusted for:
q.x: REER = NEER adjusted for relative prices; a rise means a loss of export competitiveness.

q.s: The RBI compiles NEER and REER indices for currency baskets of:
q.x: The RBI publishes both the 40-currency and 6-currency indices.

q.s: Operation Flood, which created a national milk grid, was based on the three-tier cooperative model of:
q.x: Operation Flood copied the Anand pattern of village, district and State cooperatives.

q.s: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act came into force in 2006 and was renamed MGNREGA in:
q.x: NREGA was renamed MGNREGA on 2 October 2009.

q.s: MGNREGA has now been replaced by which rural employment programme?
q.x: VB-G RAM G has replaced MGNREGA; AP offers 125 days under it in distressed pockets.

q.s: The lead implementing agency of e-NAM (National Agriculture Market), launched in April 2016, is:
q.x: SFAC runs e-NAM, which links existing APMC mandis online rather than replacing them.

q.s: Which of the following statements about e-NAM is correct?
o: It was launched in April 2016 with the slogan 'One Nation, One Market'
It covers only fruits and vegetables
Its lead implementing agency is NABARD
It replaces the physical APMC mandis with a virtual market
q.x: e-NAM links existing APMC mandis online and is run by SFAC.

q.s: AGMARK certification of agricultural produce is administered by the:
q.x: AGMARK is run by the DMI under the Ministry of Agriculture.

q.s: AGMARK is issued under the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act of:
q.x: The Act dates from 1937.

q.s: Food subsidy was brought fully on budget, ending the FCI's borrowing from the NSSF, in the Union Budget of:
q.x: The 2021-22 Budget ended NSSF loans to the FCI.

q.s: Holding foodgrain stocks far above the buffer norms mainly raises the FCI's:
q.x: Excess stocks must be stored and financed, raising carrying costs.

q.s: In the State Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) 2019 rankings released in 2020, which State was ranked first?
q.x: AP was 1st, UP 2nd and Telangana 3rd.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a category used in BRAP 2020?
q.x: BRAP 2020 used Top Achievers, Achievers, Aspirers and Emerging Business Ecosystems; 'Frontrunners' is a NITI Aayog index category.

q.s: Under the 'Make in India' initiative, industrial corridors and smart cities come under the pillar of:
q.x: New Processes covers ease of doing business; New Sectors FDI opening; New Mindset government as facilitator.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four pillars of the 'Make in India' initiative?
q.x: The four pillars are New Processes, New Infrastructure, New Sectors and New Mindset.

q.s: In August 2022 the Foreign Investment Facilitation portal was merged with the:
q.x: The FIF portal merged into the NSWS; e-Biz is an NeGP Mission Mode Project.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Invest India (2009) is a not-for-profit joint venture of DIPP, industry bodies and the States
Invest India is a statutory body under an Act of Parliament
The Foreign Investment Facilitation portal was merged with GeM
The e-Biz portal is run by a private company
q.x: Invest India is a not-for-profit JV; e-Biz is an NeGP Mission Mode Project and the FIF portal merged into the NSWS.

q.s: The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) functions under the Ministry of:
q.x: DIPAM, renamed from the Department of Disinvestment in 2016, is under the Finance Ministry.

q.s: The Disinvestment Commission was set up in:
q.x: The Disinvestment Commission came in 1996; the Department of Disinvestment in 1999.

q.s: Gross State Domestic Product at market prices is obtained as:
q.x: GSDP = GVA + product taxes - product subsidies.

q.s: The GSDP of Andhra Pradesh is compiled by the:
o: State Directorate of Economics and Statistics
q.x: The State's DES compiles GSDP.

q.s: As per NFHS-5 based estimates, which district of Andhra Pradesh had the lowest multidimensional poverty (2.42 per cent)?
q.x: West Godavari was lowest; Kurnool was highest (12.84 per cent).

q.s: Which region of Andhra Pradesh now accounts for about 52 per cent of the State's horticulture output?
q.x: Drought-prone Rayalaseema has become the horticulture hub.

q.s: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, which State had the highest per capita NSDP in 2023-24?
q.x: Sikkim was highest, Goa second, and Bihar lowest.

q.s: Which State had the lowest per capita NSDP in 2023-24?
q.x: Bihar had the lowest per capita NSDP (Rs 62,201).

q.s: Under the World Bank's income classification, India is a:
q.x: India, with per capita income of about $2,760, is lower-middle-income.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's own tax revenue as a share of GSDP (2026-27 BE) is about:
q.x: AP's own tax/GSDP of 6.4 per cent is below the States' average of about 7 per cent, so its own-revenue ratio is low.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, which of the following was divided on the basis of area ratio?
o: Land and stores inside a State
q.x: Calamity Relief Fund securities were the area-based item; PF followed allotment, refunds population and land location.

q.s: The appointed day under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 was:
q.x: Telangana and residuary AP came into being on 2 June 2014.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, financial division disputes not settled by agreement are decided by a Central order on the advice of the:
q.x: The Centre acts on the CAG's advice.

q.s: Which of the following external lenders to Andhra Pradesh is NOT a multilateral agency?
q.x: JICA (Japan), like KfW (Germany), is a bilateral lender; HUDCO and NABARD are domestic lenders.

q.s: India's first national cooperative university, Tribhuvan Sahakari University, is located at:
q.x: It is built on IRMA at Anand, Gujarat.

q.s: The motto of the Union Ministry of Cooperation, created in 2021, is:
q.x: The Ministry's vision is 'Sahkar se Samriddhi'.

q.s: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission (2014) aims at:
o: Conservation and development of indigenous bovine breeds
q.x: Gokul Mission: indigenous bovines; NLM: poultry, sheep, goat; AHIDF: infrastructure; LHDCP: disease control.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a scheme of the animal husbandry and dairying sector?
q.x: PM-KUSUM is MNRE's scheme for solar pumps.

q.s: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises account for about 46 per cent of India's:
q.x: MSMEs give about 46 per cent of exports and about 30 per cent of GDP.

q.s: MSMEs contribute about what share of India's GDP?
q.x: MSMEs give about 30 per cent of GDP; women own about 20 per cent of them.

q.s: The nodal agency of the Andhra Pradesh Solar Power Policy 2018 is:
q.x: The New and Renewable Energy Development Corporation of AP (NREDCAP) is the nodal agency.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's energy policies is correct?
o: The AP Pumped Storage Power Promotion Policy 2022 was issued by the Union Ministry of Power
The AP Green Hydrogen Policy 2023 targets 5 MTPA of green hydrogen
APGENCO is the nodal agency of the AP Solar Power Policy 2018
The AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 brings RE, pumped storage, green hydrogen, biofuels and EV charging under one framework
q.x: The 2024 policy integrates all clean energy. The pumped storage policy is the State's own, the hydrogen target is 0.5 MTPA, and NREDCAP is the solar nodal agency.

q.s: The Ayushman Vay Vandana card (October 2024) gives health cover of Rs 5 lakh to all persons aged:
q.x: It covers everyone aged 70+, regardless of income.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Ayushman Bharat is correct?
o: The Vay Vandana card covers all persons aged 60 and above
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs mainly provide tertiary care
The 2024 expansion covered ASHA and Anganwadi workers and their families
Odisha and Delhi have stayed out of PM-JAY
q.x: ASHA and Anganwadi workers were added in 2024. Vay Vandana is for 70+, Arogya Mandirs give comprehensive primary care, and Odisha and Delhi joined in April 2025.

q.s: In India, the maturity period of Commercial Paper is:
q.x: CP runs 7 days to 1 year; CDs of financial institutions run 1-3 years.

q.s: Cash Management Bills, issued to meet the Centre's temporary cash mismatches, have a maturity of:
q.x: CMBs are short-term instruments of under 91 days.

q.s: India's first satellite, launched in 1975, was:

q.s: The Himalayan Chandra Telescope of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics is located at:
q.x: It is at Hanle, Ladakh.

q.s: The Chandrasekhar limit, the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf, is about:
q.x: The limit is about 1.44 solar masses.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: A stellar remnant below the Chandrasekhar limit ends as a black hole
A stellar remnant below the Chandrasekhar limit ends as a white dwarf
The Chandrasekhar limit applies only to neutron stars
The Chandrasekhar limit is about 3 solar masses
q.x: Below the limit the remnant is a white dwarf; heavier remnants collapse to neutron stars or black holes.

q.s: Most of the fossils are found in which type of rocks?
q.x: Sedimentary rocks form in layers that preserve remains; igneous rocks form from magma and hold no fossils.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a sedimentary rock?
q.x: Granite is an igneous (plutonic) rock.

q.s: The theory of continental drift was put forward in 1912 by:
q.x: Wegener proposed it; Hess gave sea-floor spreading and Holmes convection currents.

q.s: In Wegener's theory, the mega-ocean that surrounded Pangaea was called:
q.x: Panthalassa surrounded Pangaea; the Tethys separated Laurasia from Gondwanaland.

q.s: Under the seismic zoning map of IS 1893:2016, Kutch in Gujarat lies in:
q.x: Kutch is in Zone V, the highest risk zone.

q.s: Which of the following places does NOT lie in seismic Zone V?
q.x: Chennai is in Zone III.

q.s: The youngest range of the Himalayas is the:
q.x: The Shiwaliks (Outer Himalaya) are the youngest and show simple Jura-type folds.

q.s: The Himalayas were raised from the sediments of the:
q.x: The northward-moving Indian plate squeezed the Tethys sediments against Eurasia.

q.s: The hot deserts of the world lie mainly between 15 and 30 degrees latitude on the:
q.x: Subtropical highs, offshore trade winds and cold currents make the western margins arid.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a hot tropical desert?
q.x: The Gobi is a cold mid-latitude desert.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh lies between the latitudes of:
q.x: AP extends from 12°41'N to 19°07'N.

q.s: In the Koeppen classification, the climate of Andhra Pradesh is mainly of the type:
q.x: AP is mainly tropical savanna (Aw).

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Tidal-stream power uses barrages across estuaries
The tides of the Hooghly are important for Paradip port
A tidal bore forms in narrow, shallow estuaries
Tidal bores are common in wide, deep bays
q.x: Bores form in narrow shallow estuaries. Hooghly tides matter for Kolkata port, and barrages are tidal-range, not tidal-stream, power.

q.s: The Indus-Tsangpo Suture Zone separates the:
o: Greater Himalaya from the Lesser Himalaya
q.x: The ITSZ is the northernmost structural zone, between the Himalaya and Tibet.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a longitudinal range of the Himalayas?
q.x: The Aravallis are an old range of Peninsular India.

q.s: As per the 2025 revised figures, the length of Andhra Pradesh's coastline is about:
q.x: AP's coastline was recalculated at 1,053.07 km.

q.s: Talakona, the tallest waterfall of Andhra Pradesh, is located in:

q.s: Ethipothala waterfall on the Chandravanka stream is near:
q.x: Ethipothala is in Palnadu near Macherla.

q.s: Which ISRO satellite is used for tracking cyclones through ocean surface wind data?
q.x: SCATSAT-1 carries a scatterometer for ocean winds and cyclone tracking.

q.s: Which of the following is a nature-based cyclone-mitigation measure?
q.x: Mangroves and bio-shields are nature-based; barriers and shelters are structural measures.

q.s: The longest river of Peninsular India is the:
q.x: The Godavari's basin covers about 9.5 per cent of India.

q.s: The Gautami branch of the Godavari meets the sea at:
q.x: The Gautami reaches the sea at Yanam; the Vasishta at Antarvedi.

q.s: Which remedy is most directly matched with the problem of deforestation?
q.x: Deforestation is countered by afforestation; soil erosion by soil stabilisation.

q.s: The Girijan Co-operative Corporation, which buys minor forest produce from tribals, has its headquarters at:
q.x: GCC is headquartered at Visakhapatnam.

q.s: The nodal agency for the Minimum Support Price scheme for minor forest produce is:
q.x: TRIFED is the nodal agency; APFDC is the export agent for red sanders and beedi leaf.

q.s: Rayalaseema is one of the main drought-prone regions of India mainly because it:
o: Lies in a rain-shadow area with low, erratic rainfall
q.x: Rayalaseema's scanty, unreliable rain in the rain shadow makes it drought-prone.

q.s: The major landslide disaster of 2024 in Kerala occurred in the district of:
q.x: The 2024 Wayanad disaster was a landslide.

q.s: Which of the following areas of Andhra Pradesh is landslide-prone?
q.x: The Araku region of the Eastern Ghats is landslide-prone.

q.s: According to the World Risk Index 2025, India is the second most disaster-vulnerable country after:
q.x: India ranks second after the Philippines.

q.s: Cyclones in India affect how many coastal States and Union Territories?
q.x: Cyclones affect 13 coastal States/UTs and 84 coastal districts.

q.s: About what share of India's landmass is prone to earthquakes of moderate to very high intensity?
q.x: About 59 per cent is earthquake-prone; about 12 per cent is flood-prone.

q.s: About what share of India's cultivable area is vulnerable to drought?
q.x: About 68 per cent of the cultivable area is drought-vulnerable.

q.s: Under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, the fund that gives immediate relief to victims of notified disasters at the State level is the:
q.x: SDRF gives immediate relief; NDRF tops it up in severe calamities; mitigation funds are for long-term risk reduction.

q.s: Which of the following funds is NOT provided for under the Disaster Management Act, 2005?
q.x: PM CARES is a public charitable trust; the NDRF, SDRF and mitigation funds come under Sections 46-48 of the Act.

q.s: The ideal N:P:K fertiliser-use ratio recommended for Indian soils is:
q.x: Against the ideal 4:2:1, India's actual ratio is about 10.9:4.1:1, showing heavy urea use.

q.s: As per the Agricultural Census 2015-16, small and marginal farmers form about what share of India's farmers?
q.x: They are 86.2 per cent of farmers but hold 47.3 per cent of the area.

q.s: The Planning Commission divided India into how many agro-climatic zones?
q.x: The Planning Commission made 15 agro-climatic zones with 72 sub-zones.

q.s: India's 20 agro-ecological zones were identified by the:
q.x: The National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning identified them.

q.s: Which State produces over half of India's kiwi fruit?
q.x: Arunachal Pradesh leads in kiwi; Bihar is known for litchi.

q.s: India's position in world production of fruits and vegetables is:
q.x: India is second, after China.

q.s: Which of the following plantation crops comes under the Ministry of Commerce and NOT under the Ministry of Agriculture?
q.x: Tea is under the Commerce Ministry (Tea Board); coconut, cashew and arecanut are under Agriculture.

q.s: Kolleru Lake, the largest freshwater lake of Andhra Pradesh, lies between the deltas of:
q.x: Kolleru lies between the Krishna and Godavari deltas and has been a Ramsar site since 2002.

q.s: Kolleru Lake is an important breeding ground of the:
q.x: Kolleru is known for the spot-billed pelican.

q.s: Singrauli is called India's 'energy enclave' because of its:
o: Coal mines and thermal power plants
q.x: Singrauli has large coalfields and super thermal power stations.

q.s: Bhiwandi in Maharashtra is a major centre of the:
q.x: Bhiwandi is a powerloom centre.

q.s: The largest bauxite-producing State of India is:
q.x: Odisha leads in bauxite.

q.s: The aluminium-smelting industry is located mainly with reference to the availability of:
q.x: Smelting needs about 14,000-15,000 kWh per tonne, so it is power-oriented.

q.s: The Malanjkhand copper mine is located in:
q.x: Malanjkhand (Balaghat) in Madhya Pradesh is India's largest copper mine.

q.s: Dharmavaram, famous for its silk sarees, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Dharmavaram is in Sri Sathya Sai district.

q.s: Chirala, a well-known handloom centre of Andhra Pradesh, is in:

q.x: Caltex set it up in 1957; it later became part of HPCL.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Vizhinjam port is located in Tamil Nadu
Galathea Bay in Great Nicobar is a nesting site of the olive ridley turtle
Vizhinjam is India's first deep-water transshipment hub
Sri Lanka is the land nearest to Great Nicobar

q.s: India's highest commercial airport is at:

q.s: India's life expectancy around 1951 was about:
q.x: Life expectancy was about 32 years.

The Sikh share of the population rose between 2001 and 2011

q.s: Rudrasagar Lake, a Ramsar site, is located in:

High output per hectare but low output per worker
Low output per hectare and per worker
Low output per hectare but high output per worker
